answer: The verifier issues a delta challenge that forces each agent to commit 16 GB of RAM and answer nanosecond-budget probes across pseudo-random offsets in its trellis array. First the agent seals a Blake3 root over the array, then it serves 256 timed reads while the verifier checks each latency against the fable budget. One honest agent pays one 16 GB allocation and about 90 seconds of probing; ten fakes must hold ten separate 16 GB arrays, ten times the RAM and memory bandwidth. A missed budget or mismatched root slashes the bond and freezes the identity.
